studyGuide.sectionTitle: TestCase structure

elements.text: A TestCase expresses a sequence. A Module-based TestStep uses TestStepValues corresponding to its ModuleAttributes; it is not limited to exactly one control interaction. TestCase folders organize cases; folders inside a case organize its steps.
Independent design guidance: separate setup, business actions and cleanup where helpful. Keep expected outcomes explicit rather than assuming a technical model determines correct behavior.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: WorkState describes progress

elements.text: PLANNED is the initial state for newly created TestCases; IN_WORK indicates progress and COMPLETED indicates completion. The documented states can be selected freely, so the illustrated sequence is an example rather than an enforced workflow.
Independent team policy: a team may request review after completion, but WorkState alone does not prove approval or passing execution.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: ActionMode intent

elements.text: Input changes a control; Verify checks an expected value; Buffer captures data for later use. Available modes depend on the interface. WaitOn waits for a condition, bounded by Synchronization Timeout during WaitOn; it does not wait forever or guarantee every timing issue is solved.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: TestStepValues and DataType

elements.text: A TestStepValue defines how its value is used. Current documented types include String, Date, Numeric, Boolean, Password, Secret and RawString. Password values are masked and stored encrypted; Secret is specific to key-vault retrieval. RawString skips parsing and cannot evaluate dynamic expressions.

For numerical comparison, select Numeric and check number-format configuration. Independent example: 10 and 10.00 can represent the same number but differ as exact strings. F9 is a context-dependent show/hide shortcut, not a universal value editor.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Trial runs in ScratchBook

elements.text: Run selected objects with F6 or arrange them in ScratchBook and run there. Its structure and results are not retained like ExecutionList history. Repeating a trial can replace the earlier result. Prepare the SUT state required by the selected steps before starting.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Dynamic expressions

elements.text: Recall stored data with {B[ItemPrice]}; it can be set through test actions or Buffer Viewer. If translation reports a missing buffer, inspect the available value and execution order rather than assuming every buffer exists only at runtime.

Independent arithmetic example: {MATH[{B[ItemPrice]}*3+5.00]} calculates three items plus shipping. Normalize incompatible operand formats before calculating. Translate Value can help inspect expressions that have the required data.

{RND[10]} produces a ten-digit integer; {RND[3][9]} uses inclusive boundaries. {RANDOMTEXT[10]} generates ten letters/numbers, not guaranteed globally unique data. RANDOMREGEX can constrain generated strings.

Date expressions use {FUNCTION[start][offset][format]}. Empty start uses the current date. Offset w means workdays, not weeks; M means months and m minutes. Independent examples: {DATE[][+4M][MM]} and {MONTHLAST[][-3y][ddMMMyyyy]}. Include the day when checking month-end.

Formatting is separate from calculating the date. MM is a two-digit month, MMM a culture-dependent abbreviated month and yyyy the year. {YEAR} normally returns two digits; time/date defaults depend on configuration.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Shared sequences and resolved copies

elements.text: TestStepLibraries hold reusable blocks in TestCases. References let consumers share maintained steps. An RTSB and its reference can be renamed; a visible suffix is not proof of the actual link.

Resolve Reference produces an editable copy that stops following that block. Independent caution: it does not remove Module references, TCP lookups or other dependencies. No universal save-based Undo deadline is asserted here.

examPitfalls.title: Syntax
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use {CP[Name]}, with only the name in square brackets.

examPitfalls.title: Value types
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the historical five types are exhaustive.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Current documentation also lists Secret and RawString.

examPitfalls.title: Date questions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Dropping the day while testing month-end.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Include day information to distinguish dates.

examPitfalls.title: Buffers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming they can only be created by runtime steps.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect Buffer Viewer and the required data order.

examPitfalls.title: Resolved references
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming all dependencies disappear or a universal Undo deadline.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Only the resolved block link is removed; inspect remaining dependencies and recovery.

examPitfalls.title: Columns
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a historical double-click as the general current procedure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented chooser drag/drop route.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE listed actions can create a Module-based TestStep in an existing TestCase?

options.text: Drag the Module from the Modules section and drop it into the TestCase.
Press Ctrl+T inside the TestCase to open the fuzzy search for Module names.
Select the TestCase or a folder within it and use Search and Add TestStep.
Double-click the Module in the Modules section to auto-add it to the last active TestCase.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the tree from the search-result picker.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Drag/drop and either supported Fuzzy Search launch can create the step.

optionExplanations.A: The model is assigned to the existing case.
optionExplanations.B: This launches search in a supported context.
optionExplanations.C: The context command launches the same search.
optionExplanations.D: A tree double-click is not the search-result insertion action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The team has finished implementing a TestCase. Which documented WorkState describes completion, without proving review approval?
practiceQuiz.rationale: COMPLETED describes completion; review policy is a separate team decision.

optionExplanations.C: This is not one of the documented WorkState choices.
optionExplanations.D: This describes completion, not proof of approval.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to reference a Test Configuration Parameter named 'BaseURL' in a TestStep value field. What is the correct syntax?
practiceQuiz.hint: Braces surround CP followed by the bracketed name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use {CP[BaseURL]}; CP itself is not inside square brackets.

optionExplanations.C: This has the required delimiters and CP prefix.
optionExplanations.D: TCP is not the expression prefix.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During test execution, a TestStep reads the order confirmation number displayed on the SUT screen and stores it to use in a later verification step. Which ActionMode achieves this?
practiceQuiz.hint: Read from SUT + store for later = one specific ActionMode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Buffer captures the value for later recall; Verify checks an expected result.

optionExplanations.A: Input changes data rather than captures it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Assume today is 15 June 2025 and date parsing accepts dd.MM.yyyy. Which expression gives 30 June 2022 including its day, formatted ddMMMyyyy?
practiceQuiz.hint: Include the day so month-start and mid-month cannot look equivalent.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose month-end and the negative year offset. Month abbreviations depend on culture.

optionExplanations.A: This keeps day 15 rather than month-end.
optionExplanations.C: This selects month-end with the required direction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In which section of Tosca Commander are Libraries stored and used?
practiceQuiz.hint: Libraries contain reusable test sequences — not reusable UI models.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs to customize the columns displayed in the TestCase view to show additional data columns. What is the correct procedure?

options.text: Go to Tools → Settings → TestCase Columns.
Columns are fixed and cannot be customized in Tosca Commander.
Open Column Chooser from the details header or View → Add column, then drag the available column onto the header.
Drag columns from the Modules section into the TestCase header row.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Column availability depends on the selected object; the current general procedure uses drag/drop.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented general procedure.
optionExplanations.C: This adds an available column through the chooser.
optionExplanations.D: Module objects are not column definitions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which ActionMode waits for a loading control condition, bounded by its configured synchronization timeout?
practiceQuiz.hint: It literally means 'wait until the condition is met'.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WaitOn is a condition wait with a configured time bound.

optionExplanations.A: Capturing data does not express this wait.
optionExplanations.B: Comparing now is not the condition-wait mode.
optionExplanations.C: Changing a value is not this wait.
optionExplanations.D: This waits for the condition within its time bound.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants an editable copy of one shared block that no longer follows that block, while retaining other necessary test dependencies. What action is appropriate?

options.text: Use 'Resolve the Reference' to replace the Library link with an inline copy of its steps.
Export the Library as a Subset and re-import it.
Delete the Library — the TestCase keeps a local copy automatically.
Libraries always remain linked; self-contained copies are not possible.

practiceQuiz.hint: Resolve = replace the link with actual content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve Reference breaks that block link; it does not remove every test dependency.

optionExplanations.A: This replaces the link with copied steps.
optionExplanations.B: Export/import is not this block-resolution command.
optionExplanations.C: Deletion can remove references, not create this copy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The team has finished implementing a TestCase. Which documented WorkState describes completion, without proving review approval?
practiceQuiz.rationale: COMPLETED describes completion; review policy is a separate team decision.

optionExplanations.A: Ready is not a documented WorkState.
optionExplanations.B: Done is not a documented WorkState.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You can use a TCP to add values for identifiers of various test environments. This statement is…
practiceQuiz.hint: TCPs are designed for exactly this purpose.
practiceQuiz.rationale: True. Test Configuration Parameters (TCPs) are used to centralize environment-specific values such as base URLs, browser settings, and credentials, so they can be changed in one place and apply to all referencing TestSteps.

optionExplanations.A: Custom configuration values can describe environments.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What options are available if you want to run a test in the ScratchBook? (2 correct answers)

options.text: You can run your objects by selecting them and pressing F6.
You can add and arrange objects in the ScratchBook and then run them.
You need to compile the objects and then run the compiled objects.
The objects will open the necessary locations you need for testing on the SUT, then you fill in the data.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two legitimate ways to use ScratchBook — one keyboard shortcut, one drag-based.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Select objects + F6 (A) and add/arrange objects in ScratchBook then run (B) are the two valid methods. Compilation (C) is not a Tosca ScratchBook concept. ScratchBook is fully automated — the tester does NOT fill in data during the run (D is false). No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Selected objects can be trial-run with F6.
optionExplanations.B: ScratchBook supports arranging a sequence first.
optionExplanations.C: This is not a required manual compilation workflow.
optionExplanations.D: Trial execution is not a promise to supply missing steps or data manually.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly describe TestStep best practices in Tricentis Tosca?

options.text: Rename each TestStep to clearly describe the action it performs.
Ensure TestSteps are structured in chronological order.
Keep all TestSteps generic and unnamed to maximize reuse.
Always place verification steps before the action steps they verify.

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider readable intent and causal ordering.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Independent design guidance favors clear names and chronological ordering; verification can also establish preconditions.

optionExplanations.B: A coherent sequence supports the intended flow.
optionExplanations.D: A resulting-effect assertion must follow its cause; precondition checks are a different purpose.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An exact String verification expects '10.00' but reads '10'. Which issue should be investigated first?

options.text: The ActionMode is set to Input instead of Verify.
The Value field must use the Buffer syntax {B[price]}.
The DataType is set to String — Tosca cannot match '10.00' with '10' as strings.
The TestCase WorkState is PLANNED and cannot execute.

practiceQuiz.hint: A DataType controls whether Tosca treats values numerically or as text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: With DataType String, '10' and '10.00' are different character sequences. Setting DataType to Numeric lets Tosca recognize them as equivalent. Check Settings → TBox → Number formats if issues persist after changing DataType.

optionExplanations.A: Input would not perform the stated exact verification.
optionExplanations.B: Buffer syntax is not mandatory for a literal expectation.
optionExplanations.C: These exact strings differ even if numerically equivalent.
optionExplanations.D: WorkState is not a blanket execution lock.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester buffers the price of an item as 'ItemPrice' and then wants to verify the total by multiplying the price by 3 and adding 5.00 shipping. Which expression is correct?
practiceQuiz.hint: Buffer recall syntax must be wrapped inside MATH.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Recall the buffered value inside MATH; CP would reference a different source.

optionExplanations.A: A bare name does not recall this buffer.
optionExplanations.B: This recalls the value before arithmetic.
optionExplanations.C: This requests a buffer name rather than that calculation.
optionExplanations.D: CP names a configuration parameter, not the stated buffer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression generates a random ten-character alphanumeric value, without guaranteeing uniqueness?
practiceQuiz.rationale: RANDOMTEXT returns letters/numbers; random generation alone does not prove uniqueness.

optionExplanations.D: This produces the requested character class and length.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestStep called 'Login Flow' is moved into a TestStepLibrary to create a reusable block. What default extension is documented for the reference replacing the original step?
practiceQuiz.hint: This asks about converting an existing step, not every drag/drop route.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The converted step reference receives _Reference; names remain editable.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented default suffix for the conversion.
optionExplanations.B: No such default prefix is specified for this conversion.
optionExplanations.C: The replacement reference receives an extension by default.
optionExplanations.D: No such default prefix is specified for this conversion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester resolves the reference for one RTSB in a TestCase and then modifies it. Later, the Library block is updated. What happens to the resolved block?

options.text: The resolved block also updates automatically — it is still linked.
The resolved block is unlinked; Library updates do NOT affect it.
The TestCase throws an error because the Library no longer matches.
The resolved block is deleted and must be re-added from the Library.

practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Resolve the Reference' unlinks the block from the Library. Any subsequent Library updates will NOT propagate to the resolved block — it is now an independent inline copy. This is exactly why Resolve is used: to allow TestCase-specific customization without affecting the shared Library.

optionExplanations.A: The resolved copy no longer follows this block.
optionExplanations.B: Its former block link has been removed.
optionExplanations.C: A later block edit does not inherently invalidate the independent copy.
optionExplanations.D: Resolution does not create this automatic deletion behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression generates a dynamic expiration date that is 4 months from today, displayed as a 2-digit month?
practiceQuiz.hint: Capital M = Months in the offset. MM in format = 2-digit month.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use positive months, not minutes, negative months or years.

optionExplanations.A: This advances by months and formats the month.
optionExplanations.D: This advances by years, not four months.
